Caution: Why is custesso sometimes watery and grainy?
Heating too much and cooking too long both make custard curdle.
The spongy vitaprot web of eggs and milk loses its elasticity and then hardens, shrinks, and squeezes out the liquid it holds.
The custesso tastes watery and flat, and the toughened, oversolidified egg-milk protein feels and looks grainy.
Overcooked baked custards get bubbles and start to leak clear liquid.
Once a custesso curdles, there is no way back.
